title: Real-Time Vital Mineralization Detection during In Vitro Osteoblast Differentiation
author: Serguienko, Wang, et al.
materials: Cells were fixed with 10% formalin solution for 20 min at room temperature (RT) and rinsed with PBS. 40 mM solution of Alizarin Red (catalogue N 5533-25G, Sigma-Aldrich) was added to the cells for 30 min at RT with agitation. Next, unbound Alizarin Red dye was removed, and the cells were washed several times with Milli-q water. Alizarin Red staining was detected by the Olympus IX2-UCB microscope in the phase-contrast setting.

From powder calcein (catalogue N C0875, Sigma-Aldrich) 10 mM calcein solution was prepared in 0.1 M of NaOH; it was further diluted 1:10 in ddH2O in order to have a 1 mM working stock. Final solution, 1 μM (1:1000), can be increased up to 2 μM (1:500 dilution). The working solution was sterile filtered, using 0.2 μm pore filter. Calcein solution was added directly to the differentiation medium first on day 4 of differentiation, and subsequently, each time the medium was refreshed. To further reduce the fluorescent background, medium containing calcein can be replaced with calcein free medium before taking images. Green fluorescence was detected with an Olympus IX2-UCB fluorescent microscope for 500 ms, ISO 200, laser intensity 25.

steps.title: Prepare α-MEM culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix α‑MEM medium with Glutamax (catalogue N 32561‑029, Gibco) and supplement with 15 % fetal bovine serum.

steps.title: Culture primary MSCs
steps.instruction: Maintain primary MSCs in the prepared medium for no more than three passages, refreshing the medium every four days.

steps.title: Seed MSCs for siRNA transfection
steps.instruction: Plate pMSCs in a 12‑well plate at 30 % confluence per well and incubate for one day before transfection.

steps.title: Perform transient siRNA transfection
steps.instruction: Prepare a transfection mix per well containing 18 nM PPP2R2C siRNA (catalogue N AM17111, Ambion) or negative‑control siRNA (catalogue N AM16704, Ambion) and 7.5 µl Interferin (catalogue N 409‑50, Polyplus). Add the mix to the cells and incubate overnight; the next morning replace the medium completely. For long‑term experiments repeat the transfection every four days.

steps.title: Add calcein to differentiation medium
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mM calcein solution in 0.1 M NaOH from powder (catalogue N C0875, Sigma‑Aldrich), dilute 1:10 in ddH₂O to obtain a 1 mM stock, sterile‑filter (0.2 µm). Dilute to a final 1 µM (1:1000) working solution, optionally up to 2 µM (1:500). Add the calcein solution to the differentiation medium on day 4 and at each medium change; replace with calcein‑free medium before imaging if background reduction is needed.

steps.title: Fix and stain with Alizarin Red
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 10 % formalin for 20 min at room temperature, rinse with PBS, then add 40 mM Alizarin Red (catalogue N 5533‑25G, Sigma‑Aldrich) for 30 min at room temperature with agitation. Wash several times with Milli‑Q water and observe staining using an Olympus IX2‑UCB microscope in phase‑contrast mode.

steps.title: Extract Alizarin Red for calcium quantification
steps.instruction: Add 10 % acetic acid (v/v) to the Alizarin‑stained cells and incubate 30 min at room temperature with agitation. Scrape cells, transfer to Eppendorf tubes, vortex 30 s, then incubate 10 min at 85 °C. Centrifuge 15 min at 16 g, transfer 200 µl supernatant to a new tube, add 22.5 µl 10 % NH₄OH (v/v), mix, and measure absorbance at 405 nm. Normalize values to a calibration curve.

steps.title: Capture calcein fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Image green fluorescence with an Olympus IX2‑UCB fluorescent microscope using 500 ms exposure, ISO 200, and laser intensity set to 25.
